issues.legal_issue: A killing in a sudden, unpremeditated fight, without undue advantage or cruel conduct, falls within the sudden-fight exception to murder where the offender had knowledge of the fatal risk but no intention to cause death.
material_facts: A verbal objection during ongoing legal proceedings led to a sudden scuffle between opposing groups, and the attack was not premeditated or planned.
The offender used a small kirpan in the spur of the moment and inflicted stab wounds, one of which caused a death.
The Court found that the offender did not intend to cause death, take undue advantage, or act cruelly.
The Court treated the case as involving knowledge of the risk but no intention to cause death.
issues.conclusion: The killing was culpable homicide not amounting to murder, punishable as culpable homicide committed with knowledge but without intention to cause death. The murder conviction was altered accordingly, and a sentence of ten years’ imprisonment was imposed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 300 Exception 4 of the Indian Penal Code, culpable homicide is not murder when it is committed without premeditation, in a sudden fight in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel, and without the offender taking undue advantage or acting cruelly or unusually; the fight must involve the person killed. All these requirements must be met. Under Sections 299, 300 and 304, culpable homicide committed with knowledge but without intention to cause death is punishable under Section 304 Part II. The Court relied on State of A.P. v. Rayavarapu Punnayya, which distinguishes murder from culpable homicide and explains the relevant stages of analysis; Budhi Singh v. State of Himachal Pradesh, on evaluating provocation and temporary loss of self-control in context; and Kikar Singh v. State of Rajasthan, on the requirements of a sudden fight and the bar on undue advantage or cruel conduct.

rule.if: case_is_appeal_from_murder_conviction and death_caused_by_assault and no_premeditation and sudden_fight_in_heat_of_passion_with_person_killed and not undue_advantage_taken and not cruel_or_unusual_conduct and no_intention_to_cause_death and knowledge_of_fatal_risk

predicates.case_is_appeal_from_murder_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a conviction for murder.
predicates.death_caused_by_assault: The offender inflicted an injury in the assault that caused a person's death.
predicates.no_premeditation: The attack was not planned or preceded by deliberation to fight.
predicates.sudden_fight_in_heat_of_passion_with_per: A sudden quarrel led to a fight in the heat of passion involving the person who was killed.
predicates.undue_advantage_taken: The offender used an unfair advantage over the person killed during the fight.
predicates.cruel_or_unusual_conduct: The offender acted cruelly or in an unusual manner during the fight.
predicates.no_intention_to_cause_death: The circumstances do not establish that the offender intended to cause death.
predicates.knowledge_of_fatal_risk: The offender acted with knowledge of the risk that the act could cause death.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a murder conviction for a death caused in an unplanned, heated fight with the person killed, and the offender neither took unfair advantage nor acted cruelly, the conviction is for culpable homicide not amounting to murder if the offender had knowledge of the fatal risk but no intention to cause death.
